question: What extraction yield and acid value did the macaw palm almond oil have?
rendered:
<document title="Thermophysical and Chemical Evaluation of Macaw Palm Almond Oil as a Biobased Heat-Transfer Fluid Candidate for Medium-Temperature Solar Thermal Applications">

=== page 1 ===
- The extraction yield was 15.74 ± 2.85% (w/w), with an acid value of 3.44 ± 0.02 mg KOH· g^− 1, density of 0.917 ± 0.006 g·cm^− 3 at 20 °C, and kinematic viscosity of 29.75 ± 0.76 mm^2·s^− 1 at 40 °C.

Answer: The macaw palm almond oil had an extraction yield of 15.74 ± 2.85% (w/w) and an acid value of 3.44 ± 0.02 mg KOH· g^− 1.
